system: You are a security investigator reviewing an alert. Base every claim only on the evidence available to you. Cite the record IDs that support each observation.

supporting_observations.claim: WINWORD.EXE opened C:\Users\maria.lopez\Downloads\Statement.docm, then launched PowerShell under Maria's account. The PowerShell command used -nop, -w hidden, and -enc; its encoded content decodes to a WebClient DownloadString invocation for https://raw.githubusercontent.com/harbor-dental-it/tools/main/u.ps1.
The PowerShell process connected through the proxy to raw.githubusercontent.com, and the proxy recorded a successful GET for the script URL named in the command.
PowerShell then launched rundll32 to call Init in C:\Users\maria.lopez\AppData\Roaming\svchelper.dll. The process was recorded at medium integrity and ran for about 22 seconds.

The observed execution chain—macro-enabled document to hidden encoded PowerShell, remote script retrieval, and rundll32 execution of a DLL from the user's Roaming directory—is strongly indicative of malicious activity, rather than the documented IT patching process.

Separately, a SYSTEM PowerShell task on WS-MLOPEZ-01 ran C:\Scripts\backup-check.ps1 and attempted explicit authentication as svc-claimsync. This is outside the documented location of the ClaimSync job and warrants investigation; the records do not establish whether it was authorized.

known_telemetry_limitations: The proxy records the GitHub script URL and a successful GET, but the supplied records do not include the script response body.
The supplied records do not include the contents, hash, signature, or creation event for svchelper.dll, nor PowerShell script-block or AMSI content.
The records cover only the specified time window; they do not establish what happened before or after it.
claims_not_established: Whether Maria knowingly opened the document or initiated the execution.
What the downloaded script or svchelper.dll did, including whether it established persistence, collected data, or communicated elsewhere.
Whether any data was exfiltrated or credentials were compromised.
Whether the svc-claimsync authentication attempt was authorized or related to the document-and-PowerShell execution.
additional_evidence_needed: Preserve and analyze Statement.docm, the downloaded GitHub script, svchelper.dll, and the temporary file; collect hashes, signatures, and full contents.
Collect PowerShell script-block/AMSI logs, Defender or EDR detections and process telemetry, and relevant file and registry persistence artifacts from WS-MLOPEZ-01.
Review GitHub repository history and ownership, and obtain the exact response content served at the recorded time.
Investigate the scheduled task and C:\Scripts\backup-check.ps1, including why it used svc-claimsync on this workstation and whether that use was authorized.
Review related authentication, SMB, and network activity on WS-MLOPEZ-01, FILE-HD-01, and DC-HD-01 beyond this window.
